items.question: Who is Kara Lawson?
items.answer: Kara Lawson is the head women's basketball coach at Duke, named on July 11, 2020, and head coach of the USA Basketball Women's National Team through 2028. She is a former WNBA champion and Olympic gold medalist.

items.question: What does 'handle hard better' mean?
items.answer: 'Handle hard better' is the message of a short talk Kara Lawson gave about handling hard things in life. It went viral, and she discussed the reaction on TODAY.

items.question: How old is Kara Lawson?
items.answer: Kara Lawson was born February 14, 1981, in Alexandria, Virginia.

items.question: Did Kara Lawson play in the WNBA?
items.answer: Yes. Kara Lawson played 13 WNBA seasons, from 2003 to 2015, with the Sacramento Monarchs, Connecticut Sun, and Washington Mystics. The Detroit Shock drafted her fifth overall in 2003, and she won the 2005 WNBA title with Sacramento.

items.question: What were Kara Lawson's WNBA career averages?
items.answer: Duke says Kara Lawson averaged 9.8 points, 2.6 rebounds, and 2.5 assists in 377 WNBA games and was a 2007 WNBA All-Star.

items.question: Where did Kara Lawson play college basketball?
items.answer: Kara Lawson played four seasons at Tennessee for Pat Summitt and helped the Lady Vols reach the Final Four in 2000, 2002, and 2003. She scored 1,950 career points.

items.question: Is Kara Lawson the Team USA coach?
items.answer: Yes. Kara Lawson was named head coach of the USA Basketball Women's National Team in September 2025 and will lead the team through the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles. As a player, she won Olympic gold in 2008.

items.question: Did Kara Lawson coach the Boston Celtics?
items.answer: Yes. Duke says she became the first female coach in Celtics history and spent one season, 2019-20, on Boston's staff.

items.question: What is Kara Lawson's coaching record at Duke?
items.answer: Duke lists Kara Lawson at 124-50 through six seasons. In 2025-26, Duke won the ACC regular-season and tournament titles and reached the Elite Eight, and she was named ACC Coach of the Year.
